Definition: of Hebrew origin (H11); a destroying angel:--Abaddon.
BiblicalUsage: Abaddon appears once, in Revelation 9:11. The locusts from the bottomless pit have ‘a king over them, which is the angel of the bottomless pit, whose name in the Hebrew tongue is Abaddon, but in the Greek tongue hath his name Apollyon’ — the Destroyer.
TheologicalSignificance: One verse names the king of the pit, and it is enough to know him for what he is: a destroyer, not a ruler to be followed. I believe the naming matters — Scripture does not leave evil anonymous; it names it, shows its end, and sets the Lamb above it.
